lit.\u0027\u003cstrong\u003e(CH₃)₃C⁺\u003c/s: "(CH₃)₃C⁺ — trigonal planar sp² carbon (Σ of C–C–C angles = 360°) with an empty p orbital perpendicular to the plane. It is stabilized by hyperconjugation (the C–H bonds aligned with the empty p donate electron density to it) and by the inductive effect of the methyls. It is an energy minimum: a real intermediate, though a very reactive one."

"(CH₃)₃C⁺ can be attacked by water (→ SN1) or lose a proton from a neighboring carbon (→ E1). The C–H bonds aligned with the empty p orbital point toward the base; hyperconjugation is already weakening them."
lit.\u0027\u003cstrong\u003e2-metilpropeno\u: "Planar 2-methylpropene: the C=C double bond (σ + π) has a length of ≈ 1.34 Å. H₃O⁺ appears, and Br⁻ remains free in solution."
lit.\u0027\u003cstrong\u003eEl agua, un nucl: "Water, a weak nucleophile, attacks the empty p orbital. Since the carbocation is planar, both faces are accessible: at a stereogenic carbon a racemic mixture would form (with a slight excess of inversion due to the ion pair). An oxonium ion, R–OH₂⁺, is generated."
lit.\u0027\u003cstrong\u003eIdéntica al prim: "Identical to the first step of SN1. The C–Br bond breaks heterolytically and leaves a planar tertiary carbocation. It is the rate-determining step."
lit.\u0027\u003cstrong\u003ePaso ácido-base: "Fast acid–base step. Another water molecule (the solvent) removes a proton from the oxonium: 2-methylpropan-2-ol and H₃O⁺ are formed."
lit.\u0027\u003cstrong\u003eRuptura heterolí: "Heterolytic cleavage. The C–Br bond lengthens and breaks without help from the nucleophile: both electrons stay on the bromine (Br⁻). This unimolecular step is the slowest, so it determines the rate. As the bond weakens, the three methyls flatten toward a trigonal planar geometry."
lit.\u0027\u003cstrong\u003eUna base débil (: "A weak base (H₂O) removes the H from the β carbon. The electrons of the C–H bond shift to form the π bond with the cationic carbon. The β carbon goes from sp³ to sp² and the C–C bond shortens."
lit.\u0027Dos etapas (más una desprotonación: "Two stages (plus a deprotonation): slow ionization and fast nucleophilic attack."
lit.\u0027El carbocatión es plano: el nucleó: "The carbocation is planar: the nucleophile attacks from both faces → racemization."
lit.\u0027Favorecida por disolventes polares: "Favored by polar protic solvents (they stabilize ions) and weak nucleophiles."
lit.\u0027Las temperaturas altas favorecen E: "High temperatures favor E1 over SN1 (elimination increases entropy)."
lit.\u0027Ley de velocidad unimolecular: v =: "Unimolecular rate law: v = k[R–Br]. The weak base enters after the slow step."
"Unimolecular rate law: v = k[R–Br]; it does not depend on the nucleophile concentration."
lit.\u0027Mismo primer paso que SN1: ambos m: "Same first step as SN1: both mechanisms share the carbocation, which is why they compete."
lit.\u0027No exige la geometría anti-peripla: "It does not require the strict anti-periplanar geometry of E2: the cation is already planar."
lit.\u0027Reactividad: 3.º \u003e 2.º ≫ 1.º: "Reactivity: 3° > 2° ≫ 1° (carbocation stability through hyperconjugation and inductive effects)."
lit.\u0027Regla de Zaitsev: predomina el alq: "Zaitsev's rule: the more substituted (more stable) alkene predominates."
lit.\u0027Se necesita al menos un H en carbo: "At least one H on a β carbon is needed; here there are 9 possible."
lit.\u0027Un carbocatión puede transponerse: "A carbocation can rearrange (hydride or methyl shift) toward a more stable one."
lit.\u0027Unimolecular: el paso lento solo i: "Unimolecular: the slow step involves only the substrate."
lit.\u0027Unimolecular: la base no participa: "Unimolecular: the base does not take part in the slow step."
